To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The structure of the B–C‐terminal domain of the catalytic Pol α subunit reveals the mechanism by which the B subunit tethers accessory factors and that the EM reconstruction of yeast DNA Pol α reveals a common architecture among replicative polymerases.

the B subunits of replicative polymerases are tethered to the active site through a structured but mobile linker, and that the conserved B–CTD interaction represents the core of a general mechanism of accessory factor recognition.

we have determined the structure of the B–C-terminal domain of the catalytic Pol α subunit complex, and that we have determined 3D structures of Pol α by electron microscopy, which reveal the overall architecture and the position of the B– CTD complex in the polymerase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism and regulation of DNA replication, which represents one of the most fundamental processes in biology.
the structural and functional characterization of eukaryotic DNA polymerases.
understanding how DNA polymerases are assembled into a functional complex, and how the polymerase is organized into a catalytic and regulatory module.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 3D structure of Pol α is bilobal and that the B subunits are attached to the polymerase module through a structured but highly flexible linker.
the 3D architecture is a bilobal structure, with a catalytic domain and a regulatory domain.
the B subunits are the core subunits of all three replicases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have determined the 3D structure of the catalytic B subunit of DNA polymerase α and have shown that it is structurally related to the B subunits of DNA polymerases δ and ε, which is in accordance with the idea that the catalytic B‐subunits form the functional core of the three major eukaryotic replicative DNA polymerase complexes.
the B subunits form the functional core of the replicative DNA polymerase complexes.
we have solved a structure that represents the core of the three eukaryotic replicative DNA polymerase complexes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the B subunits of replicative polymerases associate in a heterodimer that is tethered to their catalytic domain via a flexible linker.
the B–CT domain complex is an essential structural module of the replicative polymerases that is shared between all three major replicative polymerases in all eukaryotes.
the B–CTC complex represents the core of the multi‐unit replicative polymerase, and that the CTD is the main docking site for accessory factors.
